name: Sinomenine
short: A case report describes severe agranulocytosis (very low white cells) with infection. Sinomenine releases histamine; arthritis trials found more skin and mucosal adverse events than comparators.
text: A single case report described a 44-year-old woman with lupus and systemic sclerosis who developed agranulocytosis (a severe fall in white blood cells) and an opportunistic bacterial infection while taking sinomenine hydrochloride; after she stopped it and was treated with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor and antibiotics, her granulocyte levels returned to normal within ten days, and the authors advised monitoring bone marrow function and granulocyte levels during treatment. A review describes a histamine-releasing property of sinomenine and links it to allergic, gastrointestinal and circulatory adverse reactions. In meta-analyses of trials in rheumatoid arthritis, adverse events of the dermatomucosal system (skin and mucous membranes) were more frequent with sinomenine than with NSAIDs (10 trials, 1,185 patients) or methotrexate (16 trials, 1,500 patients); digestive adverse events were less frequent with sinomenine than with NSAIDs, and overall adverse events were less frequent with sinomenine plus methotrexate than with methotrexate alone. The reviewers noted poor methodological quality of the trials. In a meta-analysis of 7 trials in diabetic kidney disease, adverse reactions were more common in the sinomenine group than in the control group. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
